sketch.title: ConClip: Detecting and Rejecting Foreign Items in Edge-Deployed Reverse Vending Machines
sketch.abstract: Reverse vending machines and Deposit Return System infrastructure must accept only deposit-bearing recyclables, but foreign items—non-eligible objects, debris and other contaminants—can enter the input stream, causing jams and raising contamination. We propose ConClip, a detection and rejection component for foreign items that combines on-device multi-sensor recognition with Retearn’s five-level waste taxonomy and validation logic. The method is evaluated on Retearn’s Reklaim RVM line, which runs fully offline on NVIDIA Jetson edge AI hardware across deployments in India and Bhutan.

sketch.title: Camera Cleanliness Diagnostics for Reverse Vending Machines in Field Deployments
sketch.abstract: RVM recognition depends on fused RGB, time-of-flight depth and NIR cameras, but lenses can become soiled by dust, moisture and handling in outdoor, high-altitude sites, silently degrading material detection. We develop quality metrics and an on-device diagnostic method to monitor camera cleanliness and flag degradation for maintenance without cloud dependency. The approach is validated on Retearn’s Reklaim RVM deployments, including the Char Dham circuit and other India and Bhutan installations operating from -10°C to 60°C.

sketch.title: Custom CNN–Transformer Object Detection for On-Device Recyclable Recognition in Reverse Vending Machines
sketch.abstract: Generic object detectors struggle with crushed, wet, dirty and label-removed waste items across 200+ material and form classes under edge latency and offline constraints. We build custom CNN plus attention/transformer detection models trained on 2M+ labelled waste images from 50+ Indian locations, quantised to 60% smaller and deployed with TensorRT on NVIDIA Jetson modules. The models power Retearn’s Reklaim RVM line, achieving >90% material detection and <120 ms full on-device recognition, contamination detection and validation in India and Bhutan.
